spans.s:
himá, m. the cold; winter. [the stem
*χιμα, ‘winter,’ appears in χίμα-ρο-ς, lit.
‘winter-ling, i. e. a one-winter-old or yearling
goat,’ named χίμαρος precisely as is
the dialectic Ger. Ein-winter, ‘a one-winterold
goat’; cf. χίμαιρα, ‘she-goat, chimera’;
see similar names under vatsa: cf. further
-χιμο- in δύσ-χιμο-ς, ‘very wintry’; Lat.
-himu- in bīmus, *bi-himu-s, ‘of two winters
or years’; also χιών, ‘snow,’ χειμών,
‘winter’; Lat. hiems, ‘winter.’]
